prompt: Ana's note says "test the booking". What would turn it into a test case?
hint: Two testers following it should reach the same verdict.

choices.text: Filing it in a case management tool, where it gets an id and an owner
choices.why: An id names a case; it does not give a note a verdict.

choices.text: State, data, steps and an expected result to compare against
choices.why: Right: the expected result is what lets a run end in passed or failed.

choices.text: Every click, in order, the way a user would make them
choices.why: A list of clicks with nothing to compare against has no verdict.

choices.text: Having a developer read it and agree
choices.why: Agreement is not a verdict; the case still says nothing about what should happen.

prompt: Which of these belongs in a precondition rather than in the steps?
hint: A precondition describes state.

choices.text: Press Book
choices.why: An action the tester takes: a step.

choices.text: Type 2 in the tickets field
choices.why: An action with a value from the test data: a step.

choices.text: Hamlet has 80 seats left
choices.why: Right: something already true before step 1, which the result depends on.

choices.text: Open the Shows page and read the seats left for Hamlet
choices.why: Opening and reading are actions, so this is a step, even when it checks state.

prompt: Why is the expected result written before the case runs, from the requirement?
hint: What would it copy if it were written afterwards?

choices.text: So the run is quicker, with nothing left to write during it
choices.why: Speed is not the point; the actual result is still written during the run.

choices.text: Written after, it copies the screen and can never fail
choices.why: Right: a case that expects whatever happened checks nothing.

choices.text: Because case management tools lock the field once a run starts
choices.why: Some tools may; the reason holds on paper too.

choices.text: So the developer can approve the number before testing
choices.why: The requirement decides the number, not an approval.

prompt: Which of these belong in TC-BOOK-01's expected result? Choose all that apply.
hint: What does the case check, and what does it leave out on purpose?

choices.text: R$ 144,00 in total
choices.why: Yes: worked out from R5 before the run.

choices.text: The order is in the state reserved
choices.why: Yes: R6 says a new order is reserved.

choices.text: 78 seats left for Hamlet on the Shows page
choices.why: Yes: the seats the booking took.

choices.text: The order number is 1001
choices.why: Left out: it depends on how many orders came before.

choices.text: The Book button is easy to see
choices.why: Not what this case checks; a verdict that means one thing checks one thing.

prompt: Hamlet costs R$ 80,00. A confirmed member books 3 tickets, Student unticked. What total should the expected result give, in reais?
hint: R5: a member gets 10% off.

prompt: Which of these is a test scenario rather than a test case?
hint: A scenario says what; a case says how.

choices.text: Somebody books tickets for next week's show
choices.why: Right: one sentence of what needs testing, with no data or result yet.

choices.text: Book 2 Hamlet tickets as member@example.org; expect R$ 144,00
choices.why: Data and an expected result: that is a case.

choices.text: TC-BOOK-02, booking with an address nobody signed up with
choices.why: It has an id and a definite input: a case.

choices.text: Open /book, type the e-mail, press Book
choices.why: Steps belong to a case.

prompt: TC-SIGNUP-02 signs up with an address that already has an account, and boxoffice answers "There is already an account with that e-mail." What is the case's status?
hint: What did the case expect?

choices.text: Failed, because the sign-up did not go through
choices.why: The case expected a refusal, so a refusal matches it.

choices.text: Passed
choices.why: Right: a negative case passes when the application refuses as the requirements say.

choices.text: None: a negative case only finds errors, it has no status
choices.why: Every case has a verdict; this one could fail if a second account were created.

choices.text: Blocked until a positive case for that address passes
choices.why: Nothing it depends on failed; it ran.

prompt: SC-04 follows a new visitor from sign-up to booking. Why does it add TC-BOOK-03 instead of reusing TC-BOOK-01?
hint: What can only the new visitor's booking show?

choices.text: An end-to-end scenario needs a show the other scenarios did not use
choices.why: The show is incidental; the account is what matters.

choices.text: Every scenario must own one case that no other scenario lists
choices.why: SC-04 shares two of its three cases, and that is fine.

choices.text: Only a booking by the account just confirmed shows that confirming changed its price
choices.why: Right: the seeded member was confirmed from the start, so TC-BOOK-01 cannot see the hand-over.

choices.text: TC-BOOK-01 is a negative case
choices.why: It books successfully; it is positive.

prompt: TC-SIGNUP-02's expected result ends with "the Outbox has nothing new". Why is that line there?
hint: What would be worse than no refusal?

choices.text: To check that the Outbox page loads
choices.why: Whether a page loads is another case; this line is about what was sent.

choices.text: Because R2 says e-mails go only to members
choices.why: R2 says nothing about e-mail; R3 sends it to every new account.

choices.text: A refusal on screen while a link went out anyway is the defect that matters
choices.why: Right: the case has to say where to look for what should not happen.

choices.text: So the case has two results and counts twice in the end-of-run report for the manager
choices.why: A case counts once; this line makes its one verdict trustworthy.

prompt: Every booking in this lesson's cases is for two tickets. Why two?
hint: Look at R4 and R5 together.

choices.text: Two is the smallest order that R4 allows a member to place
choices.why: R4 allows one.

choices.text: It sits inside 1 to 6 and under the group discount, so only the member price decides
choices.why: Right: data chosen so that one rule, and only one, decides the price.

choices.text: It keeps the arithmetic easy for the tester
choices.why: Easy arithmetic is a side effect; the reason is which rules apply.

choices.text: Seats are scarce on a full night, and an order of two uses up the fewest a test can
choices.why: Hamlet has 80 and The Little Prince 200; scarcity is not the issue.

prompt: TC-CONFIRM-01 ends on a page saying the account is confirmed. Which observation is the stronger evidence that something really changed?
hint: What does a confirmed account get that an unconfirmed one does not?

choices.text: A later booking by that account gets 10% off
choices.why: Right: the discount depends on the confirmed state, so it can only appear if the state changed.

choices.text: The page that says so is titled Confirm
choices.why: The title is part of the same page that might say it without changing anything.

choices.text: The link opened without an error page
choices.why: Opening a link shows the page answered, not that the account changed.

choices.text: The Outbox still holds the confirmation e-mail afterwards
choices.why: The e-mail stays whatever happens to the account.

prompt: TC-SIGNUP-01 failed, so the account TC-CONFIRM-01 needs was never created. What is TC-CONFIRM-01's status?
hint: Was anything about confirmation checked?

choices.text: Failed, like the case it depends on
choices.why: Counting it as failed reports two defects where there is one.

choices.text: Blocked
choices.why: Right: it could not run because something it depends on failed.

choices.text: Passed, since nothing in it went wrong
choices.why: Nothing went wrong because nothing was looked at.

choices.text: Not run, the same as a case nobody reached in time
choices.why: Not run means nobody got to it; this one was stopped by a failure, and the record should say so.

prompt: A case for two Hamlet tickets booked by the member expects R$ 160,00, and the page says R$ 144,00. What comes first?
hint: A failure is a question before it is a defect.

choices.text: Report a defect: the actual result differs from the expected one
choices.why: Not before asking whether the case is right.

choices.text: Change the expected result to R$ 144,00, since that is what boxoffice shows
choices.why: That makes the case agree with the screen, which is how a case stops catching anything.

choices.text: Check the expected result against R5
choices.why: Right: R5 gives the member 10% off, so the case was wrong and is corrected from the requirement.

choices.text: Run it again until the two agree
choices.why: The same request gives the same answer; rerunning decides nothing.

prompt: Put Ana's run in order.
hint: Record what you test before you test it; respect what depends on what.
trap: Running TC-CONFIRM-01 before TC-SIGNUP-01 leaves it nothing to confirm.

prompt: A pass belongs to one ___ of the application: a pass on 1.0 says nothing about 1.1.
hint: The foot of every page shows it.

prompt: Why are cases not simply numbered 1, 2, 3 in the order they are written?
hint: What happens when one is inserted?

choices.text: Numbers alone are too short to stay unique once a project has hundreds of cases
choices.why: They are unique enough; the trouble is that they move.

choices.text: Inserting one renumbers the rest, so old references point elsewhere
choices.why: Right: and nothing warns anybody, because each report still reads perfectly.

choices.text: Tools refuse ids without letters
choices.why: Some tools number cases plainly; the reason is about references, not tools.

choices.text: The area prefix replaces the title, which can then be dropped
choices.why: The title stays, for people; the id is for references.

prompt: A case traces to no requirement at all. What does the matrix tell you about it?
hint: Read the matrix backward.

choices.text: It is the most valuable case, since it covers what the requirements missed
choices.why: It may have found a gap, which is a question for the client, not a prize.

choices.text: Either it tests what nobody asked for, or a requirement is missing
choices.why: Right: Ana's link to Shows was the second kind, and the manager wrote it down.

choices.text: It must be deleted before the next run
choices.why: Deleting it would lose the question it raises.

choices.text: It is a negative case, since negative cases check things no requirement promises
choices.why: Negative cases trace to requirements too; R7 is behind every refusal here.

prompt: The matrix shows R4 with three cases, all of them booking two tickets. What does that say about R4?
hint: What does a line in the matrix count?

choices.text: R4 is tested, since every requirement with a case is done
choices.why: Covered is not the same as tested well.

choices.text: R4 is not covered, because coverage needs one case per allowed value
choices.why: Coverage in the matrix only asks for at least one case.

choices.text: It is covered, and nothing yet tries 1, 6 or the closing hour
choices.why: Right: the matrix finds empty holes; which cases a requirement needs is lessons 4 and 5.

choices.text: Three cases is too many for one requirement, so two should go
choices.why: The count is not the measure in either direction.

prompt: Match each question to what answers it.
hint: Forward, backward, a row, or something the matrix cannot do.

pairs.right: The matrix read from the requirements

pairs.left: Is every case evidence of something the theatre asked for?
pairs.right: The matrix read from the cases

pairs.left: R4 changed: which cases need a look?
Which quantities should R4's cases try?

prompt: A case books 2 Hamlet tickets as ana@example.org and expects 10% off. Its precondition says only "boxoffice 1.0 is running". What is missing?
hint: What decides whether the discount applies?

choices.text: The price of Hamlet
choices.why: The price is a fact of the show; the precondition is about what can differ between runs.

choices.text: A step that opens the Shows page first
choices.why: A step is an action; what is missing is a state.

choices.text: That ana@example.org exists and is confirmed
choices.why: Right: unconfirmed, the same steps give 0% off, and the case would fail with nothing wrong.

choices.text: The date of the run
choices.why: Hamlet is a week away; the hour does not change this booking.

prompt: Match each situation to the status it records.
hint: Four statuses, and one that is not among them.

pairs.left: Every part of the expected result matched
The total differed, and R5 shows the case was right
Sign-up failed, so confirmation could not be tried
The day ended before anybody reached it

prompt: An account confirmed today books 4 tickets for The Little Prince (R$ 30,00 each), Student unticked. What total does the expected result give, in reais?
hint: Below five tickets, only one discount can apply.
